statement: Surfaces render through Isoloop's own bridge, `isoloop-dom@1`, with no rendering dependency.

events.why: The spike showed Remote DOM works but means about 7,000 adopted lines and five gaps to patch, against about 1,450 lines of our own.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: Shopify Remote DOM behind an internal `RenderBridge`, with records tagged `remote-dom@1`.

events.why: It saved the hardest maintenance work at the start, confined to one module per side.
The M1 spike costed both options, and our own bridge came out smaller with no gaps to patch.

statement: The worker doesn't render through a virtual-DOM reconciler of Isoloop's own.

events.why: Why not extend `legacy-vdom` and skip the worker DOM? Frameworks render into a DOM, so every adapter would need its own reconciler, which is more code than the subset.

statement: Isolates with a surface get a DOM subset as `document` and the DOM globals: nodes and elements, tree reads and writes, attributes, `style`, synced form properties, events and the input `instanceof` classes. Headless isolates get none.

events.why: It covers exactly what the Preact and React adapters call.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: `isTrusted` is always `false` in the worker, including for input the host forwards.

events.why: The worker can't prove an event came from the user, so code that checks the flag must not trust forwarded input.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: A `patch` carries `{ fmt: 'isoloop-dom@1', batch }`, where a batch is an array of plain tuples collected per microtask: `insert`, `move`, `remove`, `text`, `attr`, `prop` and `listen`, referencing nodes by Isoloop's own ids.

events.why: Plain tuples are cheap to copy and easy to inspect, and ids don't shift the way indexes do.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: Moving an existing node is one `move` record, without re-serializing it, and the node keeps its identity on the host.

events.why: Keyed reorders stay cheap and keep focus, which the conformance suite checks.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: Listener registration travels as `listen` records, and the host sends events back as plain event records. Functions never cross the worker boundary.

events.why: It keeps the protocol copyable, versioned and inspectable in devtools.
Our own bridge keeps ADR 0006's event contract.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: An `insert` subtree can hold comment nodes, which `text` records update and which are inert on the host. A `DocumentFragment` inserts its children in order and needs no record of its own.

events.why: The frameworks' DOM usage logs in M3a showed they create comments and fragments.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: A visual isolate whose `ready.renderFmt` isn't exactly the host's fmt, or a headless one that doesn't report `'none'`, fails with `render_format_mismatch` and isn't restarted.

events.why: A restart can't change which format the isolate speaks.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: Both halves of the render format ship in the host app's build: the worker half comes from the app's isolate bootstrap, and an isolate module renders into the `document` it installed.

events.why: An isolate built and hosted apart can't bring a different format, so an exact match is enough.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The fmt changes only when the record shape does, for example to a binary encoding. A faster transport keeps `isoloop-dom@1`.

events.why: The transport belongs to `runtime` and `host`; the format is what `dom` owns.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The host applies batches through the compositor only, and keeps `id → Node` and `Node → id` maps (`nodeFor`, `idFor`).

events.why: One place applies changes, so the frame budget and sanitising can't be skipped.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The host's applier takes a sanitising policy when a bridge is created, with no default, and every tag, attribute, URL and `prop` record goes through it.

events.why: The applier then can't create an element or set an attribute the host's registry didn't allow.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The host decides whether a `prop` record for `value` or `checked` is applied: an unforced value waits until the user leaves the input, and a forced one (`ctx.setValue(node, value, { force: true })`) applies at once with the caret at the end.

events.why: A render from the worker mustn't overwrite what the user is typing.
An app sometimes has to clear an input the user is in, such as a note box after sending.
events.prev: The host decides whether a `prop` record for `value` or `checked` is applied, and holds it while the user is in the input.

events.why: First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The host writes a `style` attribute through the element's CSSOM (`el.style.cssText`), never `setAttribute('style', …)`, after the sanitising policy, so surfaces run under `style-src 'self'`.

events.why: CSP's `style-src` governs a style attribute but not CSSOM writes, so pages no longer need `'unsafe-inline'`.
Style through the CSSOM, devtools' page elements included.
First released in 0.1.1.

statement: Every bridge must pass the conformance suite in `@isoloop/dom/testing` (`runBridgeConformance`), with no known gaps.

events.why: One suite that every bridge passes makes a bridge replaceable.
With our own bridge, done means the suite passes with no known gaps.
events.prev: Every bridge, `legacy-vdom` and the Remote DOM bridge, runs one conformance suite in `packages/host/test`.

events.why: First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The DOM subset gains a member only when a conformance case, an adapter test or a real isolate needs it, and each addition comes with a test.

events.why: The subset stays bounded by what's used, and the suite keeps it honest.
`@isoloop/dom`, the render bridge `isoloop-dom@1`.

statement: The subset also has event handler properties, `select.options` and its option members, `document.head` (detached), type-only `document.querySelector`, `classList`, `dataset`, `id`, `getElementById`, `contains`, `DocumentFragment` and `Comment`.

events.why: The DOM usage logs and smoke tests per framework major in M3a showed Preact and React call them.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: Elements React 19 hoists into `document.head` aren't rendered. The `patch` names what landed there, and the kernel warns once in dev.

events.why: A surface has no head of its own, and a page's head isn't the isolate's to change.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: Framework reads of members the subset doesn't have, which the frameworks handle as `undefined`, are listed with their reasons in `TOLERATED_MISSING`.

events.why: A read the framework survives is recorded, so a new one shows up as a change.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: Layout reads and other synchronous answers only the page has (`getBoundingClientRect`, `getComputedStyle`, sizes, scrolling, selection) aren't in the worker, and a missing member throws `NotSupportedError`. They stay asynchronous host calls such as `measure`, `focus` and `scrollIntoView`.

events.why: The worker has no layout, and a fake value would be worse than an error.
Layout reads stay out for the new adapters too, with no fake values, and the limits page lists them.
events.prev: Layout reads and other synchronous answers only the page has aren't in the worker; they stay asynchronous host calls.

events.why: First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The adapters support Preact `^10 || ^11` and React `^18 || ^19`, declared as peer dependencies, as well as plain JS.

events.why: Apps bring any release of a supported major.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: CI proves each supported framework major: the catalog pins one exact version per major, the adapter tests and a DOM usage log run once per major, and Dependabot moves each pin within its major.

events.why: A release that calls a member the subset lacks shows up as a red update PR, not on `main`.
The adapter packages and the per-major test matrix.

statement: A Vue `^3` adapter ships after 0.1, in M6 adapters.

events.why: Solid and Svelte compile markup to HTML strings, so they need HTML parsing and `cloneNode` first.
Planned in M6 adapters: it starts with a spike, because Vue's own renderer may build on the worker's nodes without HTML parsing.

statement: A Svelte `^5` adapter (runes; Svelte 4 isn't supported) ships after 0.1, in M6 adapters.

events.why: Solid and Svelte compile markup to HTML strings, so they need HTML parsing and `cloneNode` first.
Planned in M6 adapters: it comes after Vue, before Solid.

statement: A Solid `^1` adapter ships after 0.1, in M6 adapters.

events.why: Solid and Svelte compile markup to HTML strings, so they need HTML parsing and `cloneNode` first.
Planned in M6 adapters: it comes after Svelte, with Solid 2 added when it ships stable.

statement: HTML parsing (`innerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `<template>`), `cloneNode` and `importNode` are built in the worker in M6, sending ordinary insert records with no format change.

events.why: Built when a library the dashboard picks needs it.
The template-compiling frameworks need them, not only libraries.

statement: Custom elements and Shadow DOM aren't available in the worker. An isolate can render elements the page defines, which the host creates on the real DOM through the registry.

events.why: Defining elements needs a real DOM; the page can define them and the host creates them.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: There's no Angular adapter.

events.why: Why not Angular too? It needs a real DOM at runtime.

statement: `@isoloop/dom` has three entries, `/worker`, `/host` and `/testing`, and no root entry. Canvas and other output that isn't DOM don't belong in it.

events.why: The name says it's a DOM bridge, and each side imports only its half.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: `@isoloop/dom` has no runtime dependencies, not even `protocol`. Node ids are plain numbers it defines, and `/testing` has an optional peer on Vitest.

events.why: The format has no reason to depend on the rest of the runtime.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: `dom` owns the record types and `ISOLOOP_DOM_FMT`, exported from both `/worker` and `/host`. `protocol` keeps `patch.batch: unknown`.

events.why: The format changes in one package, and `protocol` never learns its shape.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: `@isoloop/dom` is on npm because `runtime` and `host` depend on it, but it's documented as internal: apps and adapters never import it, and its API carries no promise beyond the fmt version.

events.why: A breaking record change bumps the fmt, so the package's own API needn't be frozen.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The `legacy-vdom` bridge, the proof of concept's renderer kept as a fallback.

events.why: A fallback if Remote DOM blocked progress, and a benchmark baseline.
Deleted in the M1 cleanup once four-loops moved to the new bridge; benches compare against plain DOM instead.
